parakeet: Cleansing the nation is holy work, God's truth matters more than your feelings or your rights. After all of the monstrosities committed by Christianity, how do we not realize that biblical doctrine is literally the makings of a monster 101? So, no, Christian nationalism isn't some new extremist movement. It's the logical outcome of centuries of death-obsessed theology, authoritarian teaching, and apocalyptic indoctrination. It's not a political hijacking, it's the social consequence of tolerating death doctrines. So I want to ask this question what could be gained if we let go? If everything I've said so far feels heavy, it's because it is. We've inherited a theology that taught us to romanticize pain, worship obedience, fear our own questions, and wait for heaven while the world falls apart. But what if we let that go? What if we stopped calling death a reward? Stopped calling silence obedience, stop calling trauma God's will, and just start it living. Imagine if all of the energy we've spent waiting for Jesus, glorifying suffering and defending the Bible was rerouted into something that actually helped people heal. What could we build instead? Perhaps cooperative businesses that prioritize people over politics, maybe community-based education that values curiosity over conformity, or maybe even ethical frameworks rooted in compassion, not commandments, maybe joy-centered spaces that celebrate life, art and rest, therapy and body work that helps us process generations of grief. And maybe we get to the place where we elevate critical thinkers over charismatic performers. Maybe we get to a place where our children are safe to ask real questions, even ones that seem dangerous. We don't even know what our communities are capable of because so much of our collective imagination has been outsourced to the sky. But the truth is we are here. We exist, we matter, and we don't need a death cult to tell us that. We need a new imagination, one that honors this life, one that celebrates this body, one that sees joy, justice, and curiosity as sacred. It's not enough to leave the church. We have to leave the theology that told us we weren't worthy of life by design. So let's stop pretending this is just about faith. Let's stop pretending this is just about heaven. Let's stop pretending that this is just about church. This is about a belief system that taught people to glorify death, fear freedom, and submit to power, all in the name of God.
